2026-05-12 — Path B Task 1 (regression suite against v0.0.5 behavior) shipped. test/regression.js, 26 tests exercising all 8 MCP tools via stdio JSON-RPC end-to-end on the t2helix repo. Branch: test/regression-suite (off origin/fix/node26-better-sqlite3-12, will rebase onto main after PR #1 merges). 26/26 passing on v0.0.5 (better-sqlite3 12.10.0, Node 26). Existing smoke.js 44/44 still passing. npm run regression added as script.

METHODOLOGY VALIDATION: the tests-first call paid for itself before any v0.1.0 code exists. Two recall edge cases failed on first run and revealed real v0.0.5 implementation choices I had assumed were one way but were actually another:

1. Recall ranking: hyphenated query terms (like timestamp markers 'rank-test-1234567890') tokenize differently than expected. FTS5's unicode61 tokenizer splits on hyphens at index time but the query path passes the full hyphenated token as a prefix term, which trips FTS5 syntax and falls through to the catch block. Tests must use hyphen-free markers to exercise the clean bm25 ranking path. This is a documented quirk the v0.1.0 design should explicitly address.

2. No-match behavior: I assumed no-match queries fall back to recent insights universally. Empirically: only the CATCH path (FTS5 throws) falls back. When FTS5 parses cleanly and returns 0 rows, recall returns empty hits. That's two different behaviors in one function. The regression suite encodes the clean contract (strict empty on no-match); the FTS5-throws fallback is flagged inline as implementation-incidental and not contractual — v0.1.0 doesn't need to preserve it.

VALUE OF THE TESTS-FIRST DISCIPLINE: had we gone straight to v0.1.0 implementation without writing the regression bar, these two behaviors would have either (a) been blindly preserved as 'must be how it works' and reimplemented as quirks in v0.1.0, or (b) been silently dropped without anyone noticing until a downstream tool relied on them. The regression bar makes the contract explicit. Now we can decide what v0.1.0 should preserve vs change with eyes open.

DESIGN INPUTS NOW VISIBLE FOR PATH B TASK 2 (chronicle format + recall strategy):
- Clean bm25-style ranking on the happy path (multi-term match, TF-aware) is contractual. v0.1.0 needs a ranking layer that approximates this — Lunr.js / Fuse.js / ripgrep + custom ranking. Bridge-defer is the easy out but kills standalone usage.
- Recency boost (1.0 max, linear decay over recencyWeightDays) is contractual. Implementation-trivial in any layer.
- Strict empty on no-match is the right contract going forward. Drop the FTS5-throws fallback quirk in v0.1.0.
- Tag round-trip via JSON-serialized column → in v0.1.0, tags are part of the directory-path classification (BTB pattern) OR remain a JSON field in the JSONL line. Path-classification is more BTB-native; JSONL field is simpler.
